978.key_check: Green's preface (read 29 Oct 2026) says the Ross-Nicholas cypher is a commercial-phrase nomenclator (Presbyterians = clothiers or dyers; Royalists = registers or retailers) and that 'a key to the cypher fortunately exists in the collection of cypher keys in the Public Record Office, vol. vi. p. 42', not entirely complete, supplemented by Nicholas's decyphers; BL Egerton MS 2550 (keys to cyphers used by Sir Edward Nicholas, 1646-1658; record searcharchives.bl.uk/catalog/040-001983519, fetched 29 Oct 2026) lists keys to the cyphers of Charles I (ff. 3, 5), Ormonde with the King and with Nicholas (ff. 31, 36), Hyde (ff. 42, 74, 1649, pseudonym 'Mr. Knack') and Rowe (f. 22, 1655), and says the record is digitised; none of these keys is held in the repo. Not applied: the original figures are not online and Green prints only the plain words.
978.duplicates: known.py 'Ross' 'Thurloe': only other leads in the Ross/Nicholas run (siblings 978-987, not duplicates) and the aggregate row noted under lead 995; no twin of this item.
